No, not all human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-infected patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) should be excluded from transplantation. With the advancement of antiretroviral therapy (ART), HIV-infected individuals can now achieve viral suppression and have a similar life expectancy to the general population. 

The current guidelines and research suggest that HIV-infected patients with ESRD who are virally suppressed and have a stable immune system can be considered for kidney transplantation. In fact, kidney transplantation has been shown to improve the quality of life and survival of HIV-infected patients with ESRD compared to remaining on dialysis.

However, the decision to transplant an HIV-infected patient should be made on a case-by-case basis, taking into account the individual's overall health, viral load, CD4 cell count, and adherence to ART. A multidisciplinary team, including nephrologists, infectious disease specialists, and transplant surgeons, should evaluate each patient to determine their suitability for transplantation.
